title: Hydrogeologic setting, conceptual groundwater flow system, and hydrologic conditions 1995–2010 in Florida and parts of Georgia, Alabama, and South Carolina
citation: Bellino, J.C., Kuniansky, E.L., O’Reilly, A.M., and Dixon, J.F., 2018, Hydrogeologic setting, conceptual groundwater flow system, and hydrologic conditions 1995–2010 in Florida and parts of Georgia, Alabama, and South Carolina: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report SIR-2018-5030, map scale 1:889,000.
notes:
Multi-state report (Florida, Georgia, Alabama, South Carolina); only South Carolina content and system-wide statements that include South Carolina recorded. Plate 1 and figures 14-15 are potentiometric (head) maps, not geologic surfaces; not recorded. Table 2 and 3 values are simulated (Bush and Johnston 1988 model); not recorded. Figures 8, 9 and 12 contour labels in South Carolina read from page images of the cached PDF (SC part only); which state a label lies in is read from the map layout and flagged inferred. Figure 9 label 500 near the Savannah River left out (state uncertain). Florida-only aquifers (Biscayne, intermediate, sand and gravel) and the Brunswick aquifer system (Georgia) not recorded. Table 1 (regulatory agencies) not geology; not recorded.
Only South Carolina content recorded. Figure 16B hydrographs: wells HAM-83 and CHN-101 (South Carolina well names; leader lines go to wells in South Carolina, checked on the page image) with printed trend slopes; pairing slope to well read from the figure layout, flagged inferred. Other figure 16 wells are in Georgia or Florida. Table 4 and net-recharge values are Soil-Water-Balance model estimates and tables 2-3 simulated (Bush and Johnston); not recorded. Water use by State (South Carolina 60 Mgal/d, table 7) is water use, not geology; not recorded. Figure 15 groundwater-level change and figure 17 recharge maps have no legible South Carolina values in the text.
